docs.title: Manuel, Prince of Portugal (1531–1537)
docs.text: Manuel, Prince of Portugal (1531–1537): Manuel, Prince of Portugal( 11 November 1531 – 14 April 1537), was the Prince of Portugal from 1535 to his death in 1537. In 2004, Judy Garland's performance of the song was selected by the American Film Institute as the eleventh greatest song in American cinema history.

docs.title: Since When (song)
docs.text: Since When (song): " Since When" is a song by Canadian rock band 54- 40. The song is the first single and title track of the band's eighth studio album," Since When". The song won the award for" Best Song" at the West Coast Music Awards, with the song's music video winning the award for" Best Video".

docs.title: Henry I of Cyprus
docs.text: Henry I of Cyprus: Henry I of Cyprus, nicknamed the Fat( 3 May 1217 – 18 January 1253 at Nicosia) was King of Cyprus from 1218 to 1253. He was the son of Hugh I of Cyprus and Alice of Champagne. When his father Hugh I died on January 10, 1218, the 8- month- old Henry became king. His mother was the official regent, but handed off the actual governing to her uncle, Philip of Ibelin. When Philip died, the effective regency passed to his brother, John of Ibelin, the Old Lord of Beirut.

docs.title: Marguerite de Navarre
docs.text: Marguerite de Navarre: Marguerite de Navarre(" Marguerite d' Alençon"; 11 April 149221 December 1549), also known as Marguerite of Angoulême and Margaret of Navarre, was the princess of France, Queen of Navarre, and Duchess of Alençon and Berry. She was married to Henry II of Navarre. Her brother became King of France, as Francis I, and the two siblings were responsible for the celebrated intellectual and cultural court and salons of their day in France. docs.title: Jean IV de Brosse
docs.text: Jean IV de Brosse: Jean IV de Brosse( 1505 in Lamballe – 1564) was the son of René de Brosse and Jeanne de Commines( daughter of Philippe de Commines). After the death of his father at the Battle of Pavia, he succeeded him as Count of Penthièvre. In 1533, he married Anne de Pisseleu d' Heilly, the mistress of Francis I of France, and was shortly thereafter created Count, then Duke of Étampes. However, he was greatly impoverished by the expenditures necessary to maintain their position at court.

docs.title: Françoise d'Alençon
docs.text: Françoise d'Alençon: Françoise d'Alençon (1490 – September 14, 1550) was the eldest daughter of René of Alençon and Margaret of Lorraine, and the younger sister and despoiled heiress of Charles IV, Duke of Alençon. The sister and heiress of Charles IV of Alençon, she was despoiled of her heritage by her sister-in-law Marguerite of Angoulême, sister of King Francis I of France. docs.text: Magnus II, Duke of Saxe-Lauenburg: Magnus II of Saxe- Lauenburg( 1543 – 14 May 1603, Ratzeburg) was the eldest surviving son of Duke Francis I of Saxe- Lauenburg and Sybille of Saxe- Freiberg( Freiberg, *2 May 1515 – 18 July 1592*, Buxtehude), daughter of Duke Henry IV" the Pious". In 1571 Magnus II ascended the throne after his father Francis I resigned due to indebtedness. Two years later Francis I, helped by his other son Francis( II), deposed Magnus II and re-ascended.
